title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Follow-up
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on last week's reliability incident (spike of 5xxs and timeouts during peak traffic). Team reviewed root-cause hypotheses (autoscaler edge-case + retry storm), immediate mitigations (rate-limits, backoff, temporary routing to smaller model), and longer-term fixes (autoscaler tuning, observability dashboards, circuit breaker). Agreed next steps: share raw request/5xx logs, Redwood to run replayed benchmark, schedule SE-led architecture review, customer to open internal incident ticket and try patched retry policy in staging.
action_items: Liam: Share aggregated 5xx/timeouts dashboard and raw request sample by 2026-05-22
Priya: Provide the staging request trace IDs and config for client's retry library by 2026-05-21
Sara: Run replay benchmark against a canary autoscaler config and share results by 2026-05-25
Danielle: Confirm business impact windows (SLO targets impacted) and share expected increased capacity for next week by 2026-05-22
Oliver: Open internal ticket to adjust client's retry jitter and reduce client-side retry burst by 2026-05-21
next_steps: Redwood to increase observability retention for the POC week of incidents and provide pointers to the logs
Customer to apply soft rate limit and a 200ms initial backoff in staging for their SDK
Schedule SE architecture deep-dive (45min) to discuss autoscaler heuristics and fallback routing
Evaluate temporary routing to a lower latency smaller model as a fallback during peak windows
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-20 15:00 UTC · Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Liam (Redwood AE), Sara (Redwood SE), Jonas (Redwood CSM), Mark (Asterion Eng Lead), Priya (Asterion SRE), Danielle (Asterion PM), Oliver (Asterion CTO)

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick check — still good for 42 minutes?
[00:07] Mark: Yep, we're good, thanks. Wanted to prioritize the reliability incident review first.
[00:12] Priya: Yeah we had a pretty noticeable spike of 5xxs and timeouts last Tuesday at around 14:10 local, about 7–10 minutes of elevated error rates.
[00:20] Sara: Thanks, Priya. We pulled initial traces, saw a confluence of client retries and the autoscaler reacting slowly to an inbound traffic pulse. Might be a scaling cool-down issue.
[00:31] Priya: Right, there were a lot of retry storms from our SDK as requests hit 504s, some of the client retries had zero jitter so it amplified the load.
[00:40] Liam: Quick clarifying question — were the majority 5xx the Redwood runtime returning 503/504 or were there network timeouts upstream?
[00:48] Priya: Mixed. Predominantly 503 from the inference pool but also a few client-side timeout errors. Our logs show the error class as gateway_5xx in our front door.
[00:58] Jonas: We also saw some CPU spike on a subset of hosts — suggests a kernel/quantization hot path, but that's preliminary.
[01:05] Sara: Right, preliminary. We saw one host that hit a long GC-ish pause, but could also be a batching edge-case where sequence lengths spiked and kernels weren't optimal. Our profiler points to attention kernel stalls under certain seq-length distributions.
[01:20] Danielle: From product side, the incident caused a user-facing slowdown in our summarization feature — so some customers saw requests time out and our UX retried automatically which made it worse.
[01:31] Oliver: We need to know what we can change quickly — whether on Redwood or on our side — to avoid repeats during peak windows next week.
[01:40] Liam: For short-term mitigations we have a few options: increase rate limit to give more headroom (we can do per-route throttling), or set a conservative per-client soft-rate-limit and encourage client-side exponential backoff with jitter. Also, we can route a small percentage of traffic to a lower-memory, lower-latency model variant as a fallback.
[01:58] Mark: If we route to a smaller model, are we likely to see qualitatively worse outputs? We can't degrade too much.
[02:06] Sara: It depends on the route. For many of your summarization prompts the smaller model still meets threshold for Rouge/ROUGE-ish metrics, but you can A/B test. It's a safety valve more than a permanent change.
[02:20] Priya: About retries — we have an internal SDK that retries on 500/502/503 with immediate retry x3. We'll change that to exponential backoff with jitter and reduce max retries.
[02:30] Danielle: We'll do that in staging and try to replicate the request spike to validate.
[02:35] Liam: Perfect. On the Redwood side we'll up the observability retention for the week and share aggregated 5xx dashboards alongside the raw request samples. That should help narrow which inferences were served from which host and kernel path.
[02:48] Jonas: Can you also share the autoscaler events? We want to see scale-up/scale-down timestamps versus client retry waves.
[02:55] Sara: Yes, we'll pull the scaling events and share with timestamps. Our hypothesis is that the autoscaler cooldown interacted badly with a load that was briefly intense because of retries.
[03:06] Mark: Any quick config changes you can push on Redwood side to reduce the chance of 5xxs next week?
[03:12] Liam: We can temporarily lower the per-pool concurrency per host so the scheduler spreads load more evenly, and we can enable a shorter scaling aggressiveness setting for the POC pool. That requires coordination with your team for test windows.
[03:24] Oliver: Will that cause cost to spike? We have limited POC budget.
[03:28] Liam: Slightly, because lower concurrency per GPU means fewer tokens/second per box. But for a short mitigation window it should be fine — we can revert after the peak.
[03:36] Priya: We also saw some rate limit 429s in the client logs just before the 5xx spike; that might have pushed the client to aggressive retries.
[03:44] Sara: Yeah 429s often cause client-side retry storms if the SDK isn't backoff-aware. That's another lever — increase the quota for the route or reduce client concurrency.
[03:55] Mark: For the immediate runbook, what are the steps? SDK backoff change + Redwood temp config + route to fallback model?
[04:02] Liam: Exactly. Plus Redwood will run a targeted replay of the captured request sample against a canary config to validate.
[04:10] Priya: We'll send the trace IDs and a few representative request bodies so you can replay accurately.
[04:15] Sara: Great — do you have a rough QPS distribution? We need the inter-arrival distribution to make the replay faithful.
[04:22] Priya: Yes, we'll export that too.
[04:25] Jonas: Quick note — the profiler flagged a kernel path that degrades when there are many long sequences interleaved with short ones, which matches your request distribution where some users submit long transcripts. We might be able to change kernel choice heuristics.
[04:40] Danielle: Would a quantization change help? We worry about quality regression.
[04:45] Sara: Potentially, but quantization changes require regression tests. For now, we prefer tuning autoscaler and routing logic.
[04:53] Oliver: From what I heard, prioritized next steps are: (1) implement client jittered backoff in staging, (2) Redwood to replay traffic against canary autoscaler, (3) temporary routing to smaller model if needed. Anything I'm missing?
[05:06] Liam: We'll also send a short checklist for incident response and recommended retry settings.
[05:12] Mark: How long will the replay take and how soon can we run it?
[05:16] Sara: If you send sample traces and timestamps today, we can schedule the replay for tomorrow and have preliminary numbers by end of day Wednesday. The replay itself is typically a couple hours depending on sample size.
[05:30] Priya: We also want to examine error distribution across regions — the traffic spike was concentrated in eu-west-1, so if autoscaler thresholds are region-specific that matters.
[05:40] Liam: Good call; we'll filter dashboards by region and share region-specific metrics.
[05:45] Jonas: One more observation — there were a few 5xx that correlated with KV cache misses on long prompts; that triggered higher token compute and longer latency. The transcription of KV cache in our logs showed it as 'K-V cash' in one line ha, but you get the idea.
[05:59] Danielle: Ha, good one. So operationally what's the minimum change on client side to make a big difference?
[06:05] Priya: Reduce concurrent in-flight requests to 8 per worker, add exponential backoff starting at 100ms with full jitter, max retries 2. We'll test that.
[06:13] Liam: That sounds reasonable. We'll provide recommended SDK params in the checklist.
[06:18] Sara: For medium-term fixes, we propose: tune autoscaler aggressiveness, improve kernel selection based on seq-length histograms, and add circuit-breaker behavior at the route level to prevent a full pool meltdown.
[06:31] Mark: Circuit breaker as in cut traffic to the pool and return a synthetic fallback response?
[06:36] Sara: Or failover to smaller model with controlled degradation. Circuit breaker triggers when 5xx > x% for y minutes and then spill traffic to fallback.
[06:46] Oliver: Any compliance/security concerns with routing to different model variants? We store logs with PHI sometimes.
[06:51] Liam: All model variants in your POC are within your private pool and inherit the same data retention and KMS settings. We'll document this, but nothing leaves the control plane.
[07:03] Danielle: Great. On monitoring, can Redwood emit per-request trace IDs in the webhook so we can tie back to our end user sessions?
[07:10] Sara: Yes we can include trace IDs and correlate with your request IDs — we'll add that into the export schema.
[07:17] Priya: For the replay, do you need raw request bodies or sanitized samples? We have PHI concerns.
[07:22] Liam: Sanitized samples are fine as long as shape and sequence length distribution are preserved. We'll document exactly what fields we need.
[07:31] Jonas: Also, we'd like your permission to run a synthetic stress test that mimics client retry behavior. It will look like a DDOS pattern but scoped to POC pool and scheduled.
[07:40] Oliver: Fine but must be contained to staging or an agreed maintenance window.
[07:45] Liam: We'll coordinate windows.
[07:48] Mark: One other small oddity — some of the 5xxs had a consistent 7xx-ish error code in our logs that looked like a library mapping glitch; could be a parsing mismatch between SDK and Redwood responses.
[07:58] Sara: If you can share the raw response samples we can check deserialization behavior in the SDK.
[08:05] Priya: We'll attach a few examples in the ticket.
[08:09] Danielle: So timeline: Priya and Mark will get traces and config by tomorrow, Redwood runs replay Wednesday, results by EOD Wednesday, then SE deep-dive Thursday?
[08:18] Liam: That aligns. We'll tentatively schedule the deep-dive for Thursday 30 minutes to 45 minutes.
[08:24] Jonas: I'll prepare a short slide with the autoscaler heuristics so we can go deeper in the architecture review.
[08:30] Oliver: Anything on the cost side we need to watch for?
[08:33] Liam: Only temporary if we lower concurrency or spin extra nodes for safety; we'll estimate impact in the replay results.
[08:40] Priya: Ok we'll try the client retry patch in staging this afternoon and report back.
[08:45] Sara: Perfect. We'll also add circuit-breaker config options to the checklist so you can review.
[08:52] Mark: Thanks everyone — pretty clear plan.
[08:55] Liam: Quick recap of action items — we listed them in the doc; I'll send the follow-up email with attachments and links to dashboards.
[09:03] Danielle: Thanks, appreciate it.
[09:05] Oliver: Thanks all.
[09:06] [END OF CALL]
